intro: STL to AMF converts 3D models from STL to AMF on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to store a part with its real units in an open manufacturing format. AMF (ISO/ASTM 52915) is the additive manufacturing XML format: it stores units, several parts, coloured materials and copies of one object, and PrusaSlicer and Cura open it.

STL is the format every slicer reads (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer): it only stores triangles, with no units or colours. STL and AMF both use the Z axis up, like 3D printing, so the model is not turned; the STL's units are read from the file and you can choose those of the AMF.

You can apply a scale, choose the original's units if the STL does not store them and decide what to do with the parts: keep them separate inside the AMF when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The STL geometry reaches the AMF without being simplified or repaired. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task; they are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted when they expire.
steps: Upload one or more STL files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the AMF come out rotated or on its side?
faq.a: Because STL and AMF may use different axes. Try ticking or unticking “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
The STL material colours go into the AMF if the format supports them; STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the model has holes?
faq.a: The AMF has the same geometry as the STL. To close them before printing, use Repair STL.
